trial.title: Efficacy and Tolerability of a Simethicone-containing Evacuating Solution for Colorectal Cancer Screening Colonoscopy

endpoints.description: Adenoma detection rate, defined as the proportion of patients with at least one adenoma in relation to the total number of subjects in each study group (Clensia® Group (Group A); Citrafleet® Group (Group B)).
Lesion detection rate, defined as the proportion of patients with at least one polyp in relation to the total number of subjects in each group.
Adenomas per colonoscopy, defined as the mean number of adenomas detected by colonoscopy in the subjects in each group.

The presence of foam using the CEBuS (Colon Endoscopic Bubble Scale), in which each colonic segment (right colon, transverse colon, left colon) is scored from 0 to 2 (0=no or minimal number of bubbles; 1=moderate amount of bubbles affecting 5-50% of the circumference, affecting the vision of the mucosa and requiring additional time to wash; 2=abundant bubbles occupying \>50% of the circumference, obscuring the mucosa and require ring additional time to washing).

The presence of bubbles using the CEBuS (Colon Endoscopic Bubble Scale), in which each colonic segment (right colon, transverse colon, left colon) is scored from 0 to 2 (0=no or minimal number of bubbles; 1=moderate amount of bubbles affecting 5-50% of the circumference, affecting the vision of the mucosa and requiring additional time to wash; 2=abundant bubbles occupying \>50% of the circumference, obscuring the mucosa and require ring additional time to washing).

The quality of colon cleansing using the Boston Scale, in which each colonic segment (right colon, transverse colon, and left colon) is scored from 0 to 3 (0=poor, 1=fair, 2=good, 3=excellent). A total score greater than or equal to 6 and greater than or equal to 2 in each segment will be considered adequate.

endpoints.measure: Need for washing tools during colonoscopy
endpoints.description: Need for washing tools during colonoscopy. The amount of wash water used during the colonoscopy to complete the test satisfactorily is counted. Likewise, the volume of simethicone used will be counted if it is considered necessary.
Cecal intubation rate. The colonoscopy will be considered complete if the cecum has been reached; otherwise, it will be considered incomplete.
Cecal intubation time. Defined as the time elapsed between the introduction of the endoscope and reaching the cecal fundus.

Endoscope removal time. Defined as the time elapsed between reaching the cecal fundus and completion of the endoscopy, including the time spent cleaning the colon and excluding endoscopic treatment of lesions.

endpoints.measure: Requires repeat colonoscopy due to poor preparation
endpoints.description: Proportion of patients who, after undergoing colonoscopy, require repeat colonoscopy due to poor preparation, defined as a total score of less than 6 or less than 2 in one of the three segments according to the Boston Scale

endpoints.measure: Adherence to the intake of the preparation
endpoints.description: Adherence to the intake of the preparation assessed by compliance with the intake in three degrees: completely, more than 50%, less than 50% or not at all (Tolerability and satisfaction questionnaire).
Ease of taking the preparation assessed with a numerical assessment scale from 0=very difficult to 10=very easy (Tolerability and satisfaction questionnaire).
Palatability of the preparation assessed with a numerical assessment scale from 0=very bad to 10=excellent (Tolerability and satisfaction questionnaire).

endpoints.measure: Willingness to repeat the intake of the preparation
endpoints.description: Willingness to repeat the intake of the preparation assessed as yes or no (Tolerability and satisfaction questionnaire).

endpoints.measure: Overall satisfaction with the intake of the preparation
endpoints.description: Overall satisfaction with the intake of the preparation assessed with a numerical rating scale from 0=very bad to 10=very good (Tolerability and satisfaction questionnaire).

endpoints.measure: Endoscopist's satisfaction with the cleaning of faecal remains and bubbles
endpoints.description: Endoscopist's satisfaction with the cleaning of faecal remains and bubbles, assessed with a numerical assessment scale from 0 = very dissatisfied to 10 = very satisfied (Data collection form).

Rate of adverse events including symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, abdominal bloating, headache, chills, dizziness and dry mouth, which will be assessed in the Tolerability and Satisfaction Questionnaire (Tolerability and Satisfaction Questionnaire).

outcome.rationale: Phase 4 trial comparing two established bowel preparations with proven efficacy and safety profiles. Both Clensia (low-volume PEG with simethicone) and Citrafleet (sodium picosulfate/magnesium citrate) have demonstrated adequate cleansing in prior studies. Primary endpoint (ADR) likely to show non-inferiority/similarity. Secondary endpoints favor Clensia for bubble/foam reduction and endoscopist satisfaction. Trial expected to meet objectives with both preparations performing adequately for screening colonoscopy.

value.uncertainty: No direct head-to-head trial data; ADR estimates based on screening colonoscopy literature and indirect evidence that simethicone does not significantly improve ADR
value.rationale: ADR in screening colonoscopy typically 25-35%. Simethicone meta-analyses show no significant ADR improvement. Both preparations provide adequate cleansing. Predicted similar ADR ~30% for both groups.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT07696793 is a Phase 4 randomized parallel trial comparing Clensia (low-volume PEG with citrate and simethicone) versus Citrafleet (sodium picosulfate/magnesium citrate) for colorectal cancer screening colonoscopy. Primary endpoint is adenoma detection rate (ADR).

Evidence retrieved: PMC11052644 (Clensia pediatric study) shows non-inferior bowel cleansing vs PEG-ES; PMC12512418 shows simethicone 200mg vs 1200mg with PEG had no significant ADR difference (22.3% vs 25.6%); PMC4213938 and PMC8828216 show sodium picosulfate/magnesium citrate (Citrafleet class) has comparable efficacy to PEG with good acceptability.

Evidence role assessment: Clensia studies provide indirect_direction for bowel cleansing quality; simethicone ADR studies provide indirect_direction showing no significant ADR improvement; Citrafleet studies provide indirect_direction for efficacy and tolerability. No direct head-to-head Clensia vs Citrafleet trial results available.

Primary endpoint ADR: Based on screening colonoscopy literature, ADR typically ranges 25-35% in average-risk screening populations. Simethicone addition does not significantly increase ADR per meta-analyses. Both preparations should achieve similar ADR as they provide adequate cleansing. Predicted ADR ~28-32% for both groups with no significant difference.

Secondary endpoints: Lesion detection rate closely tracks ADR, predicted similar values. Adenomas per colonoscopy typically 0.4-0.6 in screening. CEBuS foam/bubbles scores favor simethicone-containing preparations (Clensia). Boston Scale adequate preparation rate >90% expected for both. Washing tools needed should be lower for Clensia due to simethicone. Cecal intubation rate >95% expected. Intubation and removal times similar between groups. Repeat colonoscopy rate <5% expected. Adherence, ease, palatability, willingness, satisfaction favor low-volume preparations (both are low-volume). Endoscopist satisfaction higher for Clensia due to simethicone. Adverse events rates similar, both well-tolerated.

Key uncertainties: No direct comparative data between Clensia and Citrafleet; exact ADR estimates vary by population and endoscopist; pediatric data for Clensia may not fully generalize to adults 50-69; trial is ongoing with expected completion 2028.
Safety: Both agents have established safety profiles. PEG-based and sodium picosulfate/magnesium citrate preparations are standard of care with low serious adverse event rates.
